label: Whatever is CREATURE_2 (caused in being by another) is CREATURE_1
paraphrase: Open analyst premise, the sense bridge of DISAMB c49de1e9-c34f-424f-b144-b80c885974ca: whatever has its being caused by something distinct from it (CREATURE_2) is a creature in the sense of DEF-CREATURE (CREATURE_1: ordered, as to principle and cause, to a being that causes the being of every other being, and caused in its being by it). It counts a thing caused in being by a secondary cause as a creature too: such a thing is also caused in being by the universal cause. Its consequent is the same Creature predicate as in 'Everything other than the primary is CREATURE_1' and 'The esse of every CREATURE_1 is received in some principle'; an earlier paraphrase glossed it broadly (ordered to some cause of its being), which made those chains equivocate. Read at CREATURE_1 it is derived (specs/creature-senses.toml, causedInBeingByAnotherIsCreature1) from the proved Fourth-Way consequence STMT-MAXIMAL-CAUSE-WITHOUT-DISTINCT-ESSE-CAUSE (some maximum in being causes the being of every other being in act and has no distinct cause of its being) and the weak premise that whatever has its being caused is in act as to being; its weight then rests on the universal-causation reading of the Fourth Way. SCOPE CONDITION (definition 80dea550, the same domain stipulation as 'Whatever has its being caused by another is not INFINITE_1'): elements of Being are individuated by their act of being, so the divine persons, one in numerically identical esse, are one element; the Son's being from the Father is no instance of CausesIn c x esse with c distinct from x. Read without this stipulation, with the processions as instances, the premise would make the Son a creature, contrary to the case's Nicene commitment.
